# New York Times Headline Analysis (2000–2025)

> Independent Python and NLP case study by OLIMI EMMANUEL KASIGAZI, analyzing approximately 2.2 million article-metadata records. Includes data-quality auditing, TF-IDF, VADER lexical sentiment, sampled spaCy NER, and Matplotlib charts.

The project analyzes dates, headlines, short descriptions, and URLs. It contains no subscriber or reader-behavior data. The source CSV is not distributed. The saved date audit ends on December 22, 2025. Results describe a source snapshot, not a complete archive or an official publication ledger. The optional RAG extension is incomplete in the saved notebook. No affiliation with or endorsement by The New York Times Company is claimed.

This is an optional file index. It is not a crawler access policy, a reuse license, or a search-ranking signal. The raw file URLs below target the default branch; record a commit when citing a specific version.

## Project and evidence

- [Project overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/olimiemma/NYT-analysis-2K-2K5/main/README.md): Scope, setup, limitations, and rights notices.
- [Results and provenance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/olimiemma/NYT-analysis-2K-2K5/main/docs/results.md): Exact counts extracted from saved notebook output, with cell identifiers and source hash.
- [Data card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/olimiemma/NYT-analysis-2K-2K5/main/docs/data-card.md): Input schema, methods, denominator caveats, and reproducibility status.
- [Analysis summary JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/olimiemma/NYT-analysis-2K-2K5/main/metadata/analysis-summary.json): Structured corpus stages and annual source-coverage counts; not raw article data.
